title: stream resume coordinator and compact payload clamp for gateway stability
author: Lina Park
description: Motivation: We observed a class of customer-reported flaps where long-running streaming sessions would fail to resume cleanly after transient proxy backpressure or reconnects, and tool/function-calls during those windows would either duplicate fragments or be dropped entirely. This follows incidents tracked under ENG-3821 and a customer support escalation (SUP-1124). This PR introduces a lightweight stream resume coordinator in the gateway and a compact payload clamping layer that together reduce duplication, provide deterministic ordering across retry windows, and avoid pathologically large per-request buffers. Summary of changes: 1) stream resume coordinator: adds a per-route ephemeral resume token and bounded resume window semantics. Tokens are negotiated at stream handshake and are valid for up to N fragments; the coordinator keeps a tiny replay buffer (configurable, default 8 fragments) to allow reconnects without full re-streaming. 2) compact payload clamp: a new compacting stage in the ingress path that enforces canonical payload clamping (removes redundant surrounding whitespace, trims large metadata-only fields, enforces route-level compact thresholds) before the proxy buffer allocation. This reduces memory amplification on bursty tool/fncall workloads. 3) handshake timeout improvements: backoff-aligned fncall handshake timeout and jitter to reduce synchronized retries across clients. 4) compatibility shim: small OpenAI-compat layer enhancement to surface resume_token in streaming events and to preserve fn_call ordering for structured outputs. 5) observability: added metrics (gateway.stream_resume.attempts, gateway.resume_replays, gateway.payload_clamp.savings_bytes) and three dashboards for resume success and buffer pressure. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-3821 design gist) - [x] Unit tests for coordinator state machine - [x] Integration test for stream reconnect + fn_call ordering - [x] E2E canary in perf lab for 24h - [x] Docs update in redwood-docs (streaming resume section) Commits: see commits list field. Files changed: see changed_files field. Backward compatibility and risk: the resume token is optional for clients; if not present the gateway falls back to legacy behavior (no resume). The payload clamp is conservative by default and can be tuned per-route; we do not change clients' visible payloads apart from whitespace and explicit metadata trimming. Rollout plan: feature gate off by default in main, enabled in canary for the perf-canary cluster, enable-by-default after 2 weeks with metrics thresholds and auto-rollback on >1% error delta. Related: ENG-3821, PM-212, SUP-1124.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Please add a brief note in the README about the default resume window size and how to tune it. Author reply: Added docs/streaming/resume.md with tuning guidance and included default values.

Aisha Thompson: Concerned about a possible write amplification when compacting causes additional escaping in some client payloads. Author reply: Compact stage only trims and collapses whitespace and removes empty metadata entries; we do not alter field encoding. Added test case for an escaping roundtrip.

Marco Ruiz: CI flakes observed initially on handshake jitter tests; can we add deterministic seeding? Author reply: Added deterministic RNG seeding to the integration test and reduced timing sensitivity.
QA (Sandeep Patel): Ran canary for 24h on perf-canary cluster; resume success 99.97% and no observable increase in latency for small payloads. Sandeep: Approve for merge.
test_summary: CI: unit (pass), integration (pass), linters (pass), e2e canary (pass in perf-canary for 24h). One flaky integration test was fixed by deterministic seeding. No regressions in existing streaming conformance tests.
notes_on_monitoring: Added three dashboards and two alerts: resume_failure_rate > 0.5% over 15m, payload_clamp_savings_bytes drop by >50% after rollout triggers auto-rollback. Also wired metrics to SLO dashboard.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature gate in canary cluster via deploy/feature_gates/gateway.yaml, monitor metrics for 48h, then enable by default if no degradation. Inform SRE and core SDK teams to surface resume_token in streaming docs.
merge_description: Squash-merged after approvals. Final commit message: 'gateway: stream resume coordinator + compact payload clamp; observability and docs'.
